scenes.headline: Working with Dates & Times
scenes.subtitle: The datetime module in practice
scenes.narration: Timestamps drive scheduling, partitioning and analytics, and Python's datetime module handles dates and times cleanly.

scenes.headline: Key building blocks
scenes.narration: The now function captures the current moment as a datetime object you can work with. When you need a human-readable label, strftime formats that object into a string using a pattern you choose. Going the other way, strptime parses a string back into a real datetime you can compute with. And timedelta represents a span of time, so adding or subtracting days and hours becomes simple arithmetic.

scenes.headline: Format a timestamp
scenes.code:
from datetime import datetime
now = datetime.now()
stamp = now.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')
print(stamp)
scenes.narration: We import datetime and grab the current time into the variable now. The strftime call then formats that value using a pattern where percent Y is the four-digit year, percent m the month, and percent d the day, followed by the hour and minute. The result is a tidy timestamp string ready for a filename or a log.

scenes.headline: Text to datetime and back
scenes.narration: A date often arrives as plain text, such as a value read from a CSV column. You use strptime to parse that string into a genuine datetime object you can compare and do math on. When it is time to save or display it, strftime turns it back into a formatted string, and this round trip is at the heart of most ETL work.

scenes.headline: Naive versus aware datetimes
scenes.narration: A naive datetime has no timezone attached, so the same value means different things depending on where it is read, which quietly breaks pipelines that span regions. An aware datetime carries its timezone information, making the exact instant unambiguous. The safe habit is to work with aware values and standardize on UTC everywhere in your storage and processing.

scenes.text: Store timestamps in UTC and format only for display to avoid timezone bugs.
scenes.narration: The takeaway is to store every timestamp in UTC and convert to a local timezone only when displaying it, which keeps your pipelines free of timezone bugs.
